text:
tori.p: can't get the quickstart to work locally, keeps returning 403 org_billing_missing. fresh account, followed the README exactly.
lee: can you paste the curl you ran and what env vars you set?
tori.p: sure - exported REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID from the console, then: 
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"ping\"}]}'
HTTP/2 403
{\"error\":\"org_billing_missing: workspace requires billing\"}
```
lee: two quick checks: (1) are you using a personal workspace or an org workspace? (2) any chance you have a cached creds file (~/.redwood/credentials.json)? SDKs will prefer cache over env.
tori.p: i'm 99% sure i clicked \"create personal workspace\" but i'll double-check. also i don't see ~/.redwood/credentials.json on my machine.
lee: could the CLI have created a different workspace earlier? devex-bot can you look up ws id ws_personal_01 billing state?
devex-bot: workspace ws_personal_01: status=trial, billing_info=missing, owner=tori.p, invites=[], note=trial requires card to enable hosted inference. docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing
tori.p: hmm i did create it but maybe the console defaulted to an org-level workspace earlier. i copied the id from the org view.
lee: that'll do it. The server enforces billing per workspace id. If you post the exact WORKSPACE_ID you're exporting we can confirm.
tori.p: it's ws_org_77. i changed it to ws_personal_01 and retried, still 403.
lee: check the token scope. If REDWOOD_API_KEY belongs to your org account, it might be scoped to org_workspaces only. Try creating a personal API key from your user profile under the personal workspace and use that.
tori.p: good call. created a key under the personal workspace and retried — same 403.
lee: ok next: proxy/header rewrite. Are you behind corp proxy that might strip extra headers?
tori.p: yes we have a proxy. i tried curl --noproxy '*' and same 403.
lee: can you run with verbose header dump? also check ~/.redwood/credentials.json again: SDKs sometimes write during onboarding flows.
tori.p: found the cache file after all, it had older workspace id ws_org_77. removed it and retried with the personal key and personal workspace id: 
* response: {"id":"chat_001","status":"ok","choices":[{"text":"hi"}]}
tori.p: works now. major time sink for something subtle.
lee: filing two follow-ups: (A) docs quickstart should call out credential precedence (env vs cache vs default) and how to clear cache, (B) SDK should include a structured error code like {"code":"billing_required","help":"https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing"} instead of only the human message.
nori(ops-bot): created ticket RED-DEVEX-461 for docs and RED-DEVEX-462 for SDK error shape.
tori.p: thanks! leaving a tiny snippet for the docs: 
- check REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID matches the workspace you intend (console -> profile -> workspaces)
- clear ~/.redwood/credentials.json if in doubt
- use --noproxy to rule out header rewriting
lee: great, i'll draft the quickstart patch and include a troubleshooting section. :+1:
